title: steering
description: The steering of one run, at .rn/<run>/steering.json: ost, what the run aims at and why, which the pruner alone writes, and state, where the run stands, which rn's scripts alone write. It lives for the run alone, and git keeps the history of each point.

ost.description: The run's opportunity solution tree, after Teresa Torres: the outcome at its root, the opportunities under it from the broadest to the most specific, the solution chosen for the opportunity that the user picked with its riskiest assumption, and the run's decisions and open questions.

outcome.description: Whom the run is for, and what they do once it's reached, in one sentence.

opportunities.description: The needs that the people named or the run found, broadest first, each more specific one under the one it serves. None is cut: the user picks.

target.description: The id of the opportunity that the user picked, null until they pick, so a run with none waits on the user's pick. The run's solution hangs under it.

decisions.description: Each decision of the run, as its aim and intent in one sentence.

questions.description: Each question that waits on the user, in the user's words. Once answered, it goes, and its answer is a decision by user.

issues.description: The issues of the run, by number: each that the merge closes, and each that the run only serves.

steps.description: The way to the target, first to last: first the walking skeleton for the target, then each addition, each for the opportunity it meets.

for.description: The id of the opportunity that the step meets.

settles.description: What the step settles, in the user's words.

deliverables.description: Each deliverable that the step makes or changes, in the order they're made, each after those it rests on.

kind.description: The kind of the deliverable, by its best practice's folder name, such as readme.

status.description: done once it meets every necessary condition of its kind's best practice.
open while rn makes it; trying once it's in the user's hands, waiting on their feedback; done once the user says it's enough.

id.description: O and its place in the tree, such as O1 or O1.2.

opportunity.description: The need, in the words of those who have it.

by.description: Who named it and where, such as an issue, a comment, or the user's words on a day.

opportunities.description: The more specific needs under it.

solution.description: The solution chosen for this opportunity, null unless it's the target. rn explains it to the user only on asking.

why.description: Why it was chosen over the others that rn weighed.

decision.description: The decision, as its aim and intent in one sentence.

by.description: user where it's the user's own answer, which only the user changes; rn where rn settled it.

test.description: How the assumption is tested on the real thing.

result.description: What the test showed, null until it runs.

assumption.description: The riskiest assumption that the solution rests on, with its test.
